system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Your task is to analyze the Dependency-Track Jenkins Plugin — a Java-based CI/CD plugin that uploads CycloneDX SBOMs to a Dependency-Track server, polls for analysis completion in synchronous mode, evaluates severity-based risk gates and policy violation thresholds to pass or fail builds, manages per-job and global configuration with override resolution, looks up API key credentials from the Jenkins credential store, renders violation trend charts across build history, and constructs frontend links to Dependency-Track projects. The goal is to find 8 subtle bugs that have been planted in the core plugin source files. These bugs involve boundary condition filter errors in Optional chains that change the semantics of zero-valued timeout and interval settings, a Jenkins API method name confusion that alters which prior builds are used as comparison baselines for new-findings threshold evaluation, a missing case normalization in a stream collector causing key mismatch between collected data and hardcoded defaults in trend chart generation, a null-safety regression introduced by swapping the receiver and argument of an equals() call in credential lookup, and a field-versus-local-variable confusion where a class field is used instead of a locally resolved value when constructing a project link action. All bugs are in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the Jenkins API method confusion in getPreviousBuildWithAnalysisResult() function in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where getPreviousSuccessfulBuild() was replaced with getPreviousNotFailedBuild(), causing UNSTABLE builds to be included as valid comparison baselines for new-findings threshold evaluation, which makes the security risk gate more lenient after an UNSTABLE build because the higher finding counts from that build reduce the computed delta of new findings

Identifies the boundary filter relaxation in getEffectivePollingTimeout() function in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where the Optional filter predicate was changed from filter(v -> v > 0) to filter(v -> v >= 0), allowing a job-level polling timeout of exactly 0 to pass through instead of falling back to the global default, which produces a computed timeout of 60000L * 0 = 0 milliseconds and causes immediate polling-timeout-exceeded failure in synchronous builds

Identifies the boundary filter relaxation in getEffectivePollingInterval() function in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where the Optional filter predicate was changed from filter(v -> v > 0) to filter(v -> v >= 0), allowing a job-level polling interval of exactly 0 to pass through instead of falling back to the global default, which produces a sleep of 1000L * 0 = 0 milliseconds and creates a tight busy-loop of rapid HTTP polling requests that can overload the Dependency-Track server

Identifies the boundary filter tightening in getEffectiveConnectionTimeout() function in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where the Optional filter predicate was changed from filter(v -> v >= 0) to filter(v -> v > 0), rejecting a job-level connection timeout value of 0 which in the OkHttp library means no timeout or infinite wait, causing the value to silently fall back to the global default and overriding the users explicit intent to disable connection timeouts on slow networks

Identifies the boundary filter tightening in getEffectiveReadTimeout() function in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where the Optional filter predicate was changed from filter(v -> v >= 0) to filter(v -> v > 0), rejecting a job-level read timeout value of 0 which in the OkHttp library means no timeout or infinite wait, causing the value to silently fall back to the global default and producing unexpected read timeout errors on large projects or slow Dependency-Track instances where infinite read timeout was intentionally configured

Identifies the case normalization removal in getViolationsTrend() function in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/ViolationsJobAction.java where .toLowerCase() was removed from the Collectors.toMap key expression violation.getState().name(), causing the map keys to be uppercase enum names like FAIL, WARN, INFO that do not match the lowercase keys used in the putIfAbsent defaults on subsequent lines, resulting in the violation trend chart always showing zero violations because the UI reads the lowercase keys which only contain the zero defaults

Identifies the null-safety regression in lookupApiKey() function in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DescriptorImpl.java where the equals() call was changed from c.getId().equals(credentialId) to credentialId.equals(c.getId()), swapping the receiver so that when credentialId is null which occurs when no API key credential is configured either globally or per-job, the call throws a NullPointerException instead of safely returning false

Identifies the field-versus-local-variable confusion in publishAnalysisResult() function in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where the class field projectId is used instead of the local variable effectiveProjectId when constructing the ResultLinkAction, causing the project link to contain a null or blank project UUID in name-plus-version configuration mode because the resolved UUID from lookupProjectId() stored in effectiveProjectId is not used
